newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar drifts in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar drifts in quiet trading.

text.p: The Canadian dollar stayed flat Monday to close at C$1.3706 (US$0.7296) in slow trading, dealers said.
"There's no news that's come out to impact on the market," said one trader.
With a bank holiday in England and the Labor Day holiday weekend on the horizon in North America, the market has slipped into an end-of-summer slumber, dealers said.
"I think things are going to pick up as we get through Labor Day," said another dealer.
All eyes are on economic data expected later this week.
Canadian and U.S. GDP reports are expected Friday, and Canada's current account numbers are set to come out the same day.
The market is especially concerned with the current account numbers, said one trader.
"It looks as though people have discounted a surplus, or at least a flat number," he said. "If it's a deficit, I think Canada (the Canadian dollar) might ease on that."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.0792 marks from Monday's open bid of 1.0780 marks. The currency was up to 78.55 yen up from 78.47 yen.
